question: Should OpenClaw core provide a general agent-origin attestation mechanism for outbound HTTP requests, and what trust model and outbound paths should it cover?
rationale: The request creates a public identity and signing boundary across privacy, config, skill metadata, plugin APIs, and outbound request semantics, so implementation needs maintainer security/product intent first.

options.title: Design Core Attestation
options.body: Define an opt-in, domain-scoped core contract with static and signed semantics, key and audience handling, docs, schema coverage, and non-leakage tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Attribution Provider-Scoped
options.body: Treat current provider attribution and provider request-header controls as the supported path and decline general arbitrary-HTTP agent attestation for now.

options.title: Route Through Plugins Or ClawHub
options.body: Require external services to use plugin, skill, MCP, or service-level handshakes unless a missing generic core API is identified and approved.

recommendation.title: Design Core Attestation
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in, domain-scoped core contract with static and signed semantics, key and audience handling, docs, schema coverage, and non-leakage tests before implementation.
